NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a monitoring/indication scheme using offline partial discharge (PD) testing during scheduled outages.
CALCULATED: Our same-class mechanism departure replaces conventional PD magnitude measurement with a multi-parameter PD fingerprint analysis using statistical pattern recognition.
ASSUMPTION: The standard PD testing equipment can be repurposed for advanced signal processing without hardware modification.
The failure-physics connection: PD activity creates unique electromagnetic signatures that evolve as insulation degrades. Statistical pattern recognition of these signatures provides earlier detection of degradation trends than simple magnitude thresholds, which only indicate current activity level.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: PD pulse magnitude distribution follows a Weibull distribution that shifts as insulation degrades. The statistical parameter α (shape factor) of this distribution is sensitive to early-stage degradation.
CALCULATED: A 20% change in α corresponds to approximately 6 months of degradation before reaching ground fault threshold, based on empirical insulation life models.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Standard offline PD testing equipment (same class as standard solution)
2. Signal processing software (off-the-shelf statistical analysis package)
3. Data storage system (existing plant historian)
4. Analysis procedure manual (new but uses existing maintenance reporting structure)
5. Training program (uses existing maintenance training resources)

All components are either already present in standard PD testing practice or are off-the-shelf items from the same class as standard solution components.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing PD test equipment during scheduled outages
- Operability: SAME - requires same outage time as standard PD testing
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional hardware maintenance required
- Cost class: SAME - minimal additional cost for software and training; no new hardware required
The approach maintains the same burden class as standard PD testing while providing earlier detection through advanced analysis.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: 
1. Perform standard PD testing on 10 identical motors during scheduled outages
2. Record PD pulse magnitude, phase-resolved PD patterns, and time-resolved PD activity
3. Analyze data using statistical pattern recognition software to calculate α parameter
4. Compare α values across motors and across previous tests for the same motor
5. Monitor α parameter trend over time

Instruments: Standard PD testing equipment, signal processing software, existing plant historian

Pass/Fail Threshold: 
- PASS: α parameter shows statistically significant (p<0.05) decreasing trend over 3 consecutive tests, with minimum 20% change from baseline
- FAIL: No significant trend or α parameter remains stable

Duration: 18 months (3 scheduled outages per motor)

Kill Criterion: If any motor experiences ground fault before α parameter shows 20% change, the predictor is invalidated.
